text:
arjun: incident-bot paging: observed sustained p99 spike on inference-gateway, streaming stalls reported by customers. alert: inference-gateway.p99 > 6s, p95 ~350ms, error-rate +0.8%. triggering oncall.
incident-bot: Created INC-2026-0315-87 · Severity: P1 · Notified: @sre-oncall @maria · Links: metrics/dashboard/INC-87 · Auto-run: initial triage checks started.
sre-oncall: ack. jumping in. pulling p95/p99 across regions now. which customers are impacted?
arjun: early list from spike correlator: AcmeFlow, NimbusAnalytics streaming calls are seeing stalls (partial responses / hung tails). ~12% of active streaming sessions show >2s extra tail.
maria: I rolled a config flag ~2h ago related to prefix-cache routing (ff/route-cache-eval). rolling back now if that's suspicious. also checking configfetch latencies.
kai: DB telemetry — tokenstore auth DB shows connection pool saturation in us-west-2; 95th CPU on tokenstore pods at 92%. seeing many repeated auth fetches: logs show bursts of `GET /auth/token` returning 429 from the auth-rate-limiter.
eli: runtime view — KV cache miss rate up significantly, continuous batching backlog length increased, streaming tail latency correlated with token fetch timeouts. suggests frequent auth failures cause repeated reauth and block KV cache warms.
sre-oncall: running quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle client retry & increase token cache TTL temporarily 2) route small fraction of production streaming to dedicated capacity fallback 3) roll back ff/route-cache-eval if it looks causal. doing 1 & 2 now.
eli: to route traffic, pushing a short-lived routing override to 10% fallback model:
```
# route 10% streaming -> rdl-small-fallback
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/ops/route-override \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","override":{"model":"rdl-small-fallback","weight":0.10}}'
```
arjun: done the API call (response 200). monitoring.
ops-bot: route-override canary applied by arjun (change-id ch-8791). Autoscale: no changes.
maria: rolling back ff/route-cache-eval now.
incident-bot: deploybot: rollback of feature flag ff/route-cache-eval initiated by maria.
kai: tokenstore pod screenshots: restarting 2 of 4 tokenstore replicas to reclaim stuck connections. running `kubectl rollout restart deployment/tokenstore -n infra`.
eli: heatmap update — p99 down from 6.3s to ~3.2s after routing 10% away, p95 stable. streaming stall rate dropping to ~7%. keep an eye.
sre-oncall: also bumping auth token TTL from 60s -> 300s as temporary mitigation to reduce auth DB pressure. patched edge auth service config: `auth.token_ttl=300`.
devex: CS notified via status page draft: "We are investigating streaming latency issues impacting a subset of customers. Mitigations are in progress." asking for list of affected tenants for targeted outreach.
cs-liaison: pinged AcmeFlow + NimbusAnalytics, sent temporary mitigation steps and offered throttled traffic migration to dedicated capacity.
kai: after restarts, tokenstore CPU stabilized to ~48% on restarted pods. DB connections reduced by ~40%. seeing fewer 429s.
eli: we still have elevated KV cache cold misses — likely some prefix-cache evaluation was causing cache churn. need heap/GC traces from runtime if we see repeat.
sre-oncall: current status: p99 trending down ~2.1s, p95 ~300ms, error-rate returning to baseline. customer impact reduced but not fully cleared. recommending extended mitigation window 45m. escalate to DB infra if tokenstore returns >70% CPU.
maria: leaving oncall in 20m; handing off to eli for next 1h. maria -> eli: please continue DB follow-up, collect tokenstore thread dumps, and coordinate postmortem.
eli: taking handoff. notes: collect heap profiles, KV cache metrics, recent feature flag rollout history, and routing overrides (ch-8791). I'll keep CS looped.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-0315-87 status updated: Mitigated -> Monitoring. assigned: eli, kai.
sre-oncall: creating incident ticket in tracker with timeline + PSR template. action items: 1) full postmortem if recurrence 2) validate configfetch client-side caching 3) add circuit-breaker on auth token fetch 4) revert any aggressive prefix-eval logic.
arjun: quick recommended followups for the postmortem: include query showing auth call burst, sequence of feature flag rollout times, and traffic routing override footprint. also consider permanent TTL change or token cache sharding.
cs-liaison: customers notified update: "Partial mitigation applied; engineering monitoring. We'll provide ETA in next 60m."
eli: leaving logs for next oncall: last 1h of `gateway`, `tokenstore`, `configfetch` logs archived at s3://incidents/INC-87/logs.tar.gz.
sre-oncall: handoff complete. eli now owner. tagging #postmortems once root cause clearer. :thumbsup:
